 J U D G M E N T

This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .1,00,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 30.06.2022 at about 11.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his Bajaj Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-01-JF-1437 along with one Mr.Harish Kumar, from Chikkaballapur towards Bengaluru on the left side of the road and when they reached near Doddaballapura Circle, BB Road, Devanahalli, a TATA Goods Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14-A-6262, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to said accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, petitioner was shifted to Manasa Hospital and then shifted to Aster CMI Hospital and later shifted to Apollo Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .13,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing CCTV Sales and service under the name and style of BS Solutions and earning a sum of .50,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Tata Goods Vehicle by its driver.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of service of notice, 1st respondent appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed written statement.

The 2nd respondent did not appear before the tribunal in spite of service of notice and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
4.
In the Written Statement, respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 has denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further, respondent No.1 admitted the aspect of issue of policy of insurance with respect to the vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14-A-6262 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the rider of motor cycle was solely responsible for accident, who hit the lorry from behind and the driver of lorry was in no way responsible for accident.
Further contended that the driver of lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further the lorry was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:

sentences.text:
1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 30.06.2022 at about 11.00 p.m., near Doddaballapura Circle, B.B.Road,
Devanahalli, when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-01-JF-1437 along with pillion rider, due to the negligently parking of Tata Goods vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14-A-6262 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner himself got examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments on the both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner contended that on 30.06.2022 at about 11.00 p.m., accident occurred near Doddaballapura Circle, B.B.Road, Devanahalli, when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-01-JF-1437 along with pillion rider, due to the negligent parking of Tata goods vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14-A-6262 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Tata goods vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14- A-6262 by its driver, the petitioner himself got examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of Tata goods vehicle by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner.
Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.
11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2, friend of petitioner by name Sri.Harish Kumar.
S has lodged the complaint with the police on 01.07.2022 with respect to the accident occurred on 30.06.2022.

On the basis of first information lodged by friend of petitioner, the police registered the FIR as per Bharath V vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83553057/
3 Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.

sentences.text: In the complaint as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part driver of water tanker.
Ex.P.3 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to vehicles are mentioned.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.

The I.O.,
after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 283, 337 & 338 of IPC, which is marked as Ex.P.5.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Tata Goods Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14-A-6262 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.

14. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained lacerated wound over lower lip,
behind left ear, degloving injury to left leg, lacerated wound present over left knee, head injury with CSF Rhilorrhoea and contusion around left eye.

In order to prove the injuries, petitioner has produced Ex.P.4 - wound certificate issued by Aster EMI Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein the doctor opined that injury No.1 to 4 and 6 are simple in nature and injury No.5 (a) to (e) are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7, discharge summaries issued by Apollo Hospital and Aster EMI Hospital, wherein doctor diagnosed that petitioner has sustained head injury with CSF Rhinorrhoea, left knee and leg degloving with lower lip and left angle of mouth and also diagnosed TBI with post traumatic CSF rhinorrheoa with frontal sinus and spehenoid fracture pneumocephalus and laceration left post auricular region and lip, left knee and leg degloving injury and he took treatment from 02.07.2022 to 07.07.2022 and again from 01.07.2022 and discharge on 02.07.2022 i.e., for a period of 07 days.

In order to prove disability, the petitioner neither produced Bharath V vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83553057/
4 disability certificate nor examined the doctor.

sentences.text: The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to ascertain and adjudicate the aspect of disability, as contended by him.

The petitioner has produced 13 medical bills which are marked as Ex.P.8 and the bills amount to a sum of .2,10,011/-
and 2 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.9.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut the medical bills furnished by petitioner.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to controvert or rebut the bills furnished by petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the aspect of disability.
The petitioner also not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .3,00,000/- (including medical bills).
15.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of TATA Goods Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-14- A-6262.
The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective policy of insurance as on the date of accident.
Further, driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
So, the respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally, liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in Bharath V vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83553057/
